claims.text: Dynamic surface restructuring governs the exceptional catalytic performance of Pt-group nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
High anodic potential pulses induce transient formation of oxidized surface sites.
Transient oxidized surface sites modulate the binding of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Formation of transient oxidized sites enhances catalytic activity.
Formation of transient oxidized sites enhances product selectivity.
Formation of transient oxidized sites enhances catalyst durability.
Under mild steady-state potentials, the catalyst surface remains predominantly metallic.
Catalytic performance is lower under mild steady-state potentials than under high-potential pulsing.
Changes in Pt oxidation state can indicate the transient formation of oxidized surface sites.
High anodic potentials restructure the catalyst surface by creating transient oxidized domains.
Oxidized domains alter intermediate adsorption energies and thereby steer the ethanol-oxidation pathway.
Potential-step experiments will produce a transient increase in oxidized Pt species.
The transient increase in oxidized Pt species will coincide with enhanced formation of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Potential pulsing will improve catalytic performance relative to a mild steady-state baseline.
The proposed mechanism should be negligible under static low-potential conditions because surface restructuring does not occur there.
The magnitude of the performance change and its relationship to product selectivity may depend on pulse duration, electrolyte composition, and temperature.
